chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Ash'ari, from Samakah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not send any Prophet or Imam except that he is the most knowledgeable of the people regarding Allah's affairs, the best in them, and the most perceptive of them.'
He said: 'And they have no doubt or uncertainty regarding that, except that they fear being tested by it, or killed in it, or having an enemy established against them regarding it.'
He said: 'When that is the case, then he is the most deserving of the people of Allah's affairs, and the most rightful regarding it.'
He said: 'And he is the one who calls to Allah, clarifies their religion to them, and teaches them His Book and Wisdom.'
ai.seo_question: What are the qualities of Prophets and Imams regarding knowledge of Allah's affairs?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this hadith to articulate the doctrine of *Ismah* (infallibility), distinguishing the absolute certainty of the Ahl al-Bayt from the general prophetic experience. It underscores their unique epistemic authority as the sole valid interpreters of divine will, thereby justifying their role as the indispensable guides for the Muslim community after the Prophet.
